body:
Building an operation request freezes its features. For a concrete collection without defaults, the conversion currently creates an intermediate dictionary and feature iterator before constructing the immutable snapshot. The standard request path repeats this cost.

This PR freezes the private concrete dictionary directly when defaults are absent. Frozen representation, comparer, ownership, sealing/revision and layered/custom fallbacks are preserved.

### Benchmarks

The actual construction method freezes each freshly prepared source once; preparation and validation are outside measurement. First-use Keys/Values wrappers are included. Release .NET 10.0.12 ARM64, server/concurrent GC, four cores: one launch per variant/policy, seven internal windows of 4,096 operations. Timing uses default GC; separate allocation runs use `DOTNET_GCDynamicAdaptationMode=0`. Ratios are PR/baseline; timing values are window medians, not independent launch replications.

Baseline `9a563e814f` C# matches current main `706ec84ff2`; only Features DLL/PDB changes in the consumer. The clean branch preserves the measured candidate’s production/test blobs (`f37a99edcd`). B/op means scoped executing-thread allocation, calibrated by exact escaping 48/1,048 B controls and zero observer brackets. Both strict process censuses failed with +336 B batch residuals; process/default-HTTP totals remain unvalidated.

| Case | Baseline ns | PR ns | Time C/B | Baseline B/op | PR B/op | Alloc C/B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Empty, unmaterialized | 3.61 | 3.61 | 1.000 | 0 | 0 | n/a (0/0) |
| Empty, materialized | 4.32 | 4.32 | 1.000 | 0 | 0 | n/a (0/0) |
| 3 keys | 163.75 | 74.56 | 0.455 | 528 | 216 | 0.409 |
| 4 keys | 161.94 | 61.89 | 0.382 | 792 | 232 | 0.293 |
| 8 keys | 478.10 | 276.20 | 0.578 | 2024 | 936 | 0.462 |
| 32 keys | 2225.17 | 1731.93 | 0.778 | 7704 | 5528 | 0.718 |
| Layered 3 over 3 | 886.06 | 860.50 | 0.971 | 2064 | 2064 | 1.000 |
| Custom 4, duplicate | 149.68 | 181.03 | 1.209 | 728 | 728 | 1.000 |
| Frozen lookup control | 24.24 | 17.38 | 0.717 | 0 | 0 | n/a (0/0) |

Three-key construction saves 312 scoped bytes (59.1%). Small-source wrappers still cost 48 B. Some timing windows contain GC. Custom fallback moved +31.35 ns (+20.94%), while the unchanged lookup control moved -28.30%; these observations limit causal timing precision.

Release builds passed; fifteen new contracts passed on candidate/frozen baseline, plus eleven existing tests. Coverage includes ownership, builder reuse, sealing/revision, equality, ordering and defaults.

[Method results and reproduction](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/da82b30d00b3187bced84dfa649bf4b839ffe9c1/performance/fusion-fresh-alloc/FEATURE-SNAPSHOT-RESULT.md), [HTTP results and limits](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/da82b30d00b3187bced84dfa649bf4b839ffe9c1/performance/fusion-fresh-alloc/SNAPSHOT-HTTP-RESULT.md).

### HTTP revalidation

Fresh matched controls use the original frozen baseline `9a563e814f`, Release .NET 10.0.12 ARM64, default server/concurrent GC, four logical CPUs assigned to the gateway, 200 requests/s, 64 VUs and a fixed 4 ms source delay. Each fresh gateway gets 60 s warmup and 60 s measured traffic. One unchanged source process spans the balanced schedule: baseline, snapshot, enumeration, iterator, scope, baseline, scope, iterator, enumeration, snapshot, baseline. Only the candidate assembly/PDB differs from the frozen baseline.

All response, identity, request-accounting and CPU-counter checks passed, with zero errors or dropped starts. Every measured group completed 12,001 requests except enumeration run 2, which completed 12,000. CPU uses actual completions. No profiler ran; identical one-second state/process observations remained enabled. Native latency samples were checked against completion counts. Effective DATAS/heap count was not exposed and is not inferred.

| Run | CPU ms/request | CPU C/B, both surrounding controls | p95 ms | p99 ms | p99.9 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline-1 | 0.841673 | - | 10.296 | 12.653 | 19.686 |
| snapshot-1 | 0.871503 | 1.0354–1.0510 | 10.230 | 12.487 | 19.254 |
| baseline-2 | 0.829226 | - | 9.834 | 11.829 | 16.288 |
| snapshot-2 | 0.866546 | 1.0450–1.0726 | 10.128 | 12.409 | 15.949 |
| baseline-3 | 0.807881 | - | 10.050 | 12.369 | 20.243 |

Baseline CPU declined 4.01% across the campaign. Ratios show both surrounding controls without correcting away that drift. Requests and five-second blocks are dependent observations, not independent process launches. Matching-window OS/runtime checks validate the CPU counter; their bounds are not full-phase performance error bars. The comparison does not identify JIT or GC as a cause.

[Matched HTTP results, raw data and reproduction](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/1e75ce82d3ec18dea4b2083272e0e946ab7c0872/performance/fusion-fresh-alloc/SHARED-HTTP-REVALIDATION-RESULT.md).

### Verdict

**Abandoned because matched HTTP validation repeatedly increased CPU/request.** The first run used 3.54–5.10% more CPU than its two surrounding baselines; the reversed-order run used 4.50–7.26% more. Both exceeded every baseline in the campaign. The measured construction allocation savings do not justify this request-level CPU cost. The PR is closed; the earlier time-separated +21.24% result is superseded by this matched comparison.
title: Reduce feature snapshot allocations
